Subject: ClearHorizon technical discovery — SDK setup, routing policies, and fallback options

Alex / Maya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can align on implementation scope. High-level notes: 

- Integration goals: embed Redwood inference for customer support summarization and an internal search reranker across multi-region traffic. 
- Primary constraints: sub-150ms p50 latency for chat-like summarization, strict data residency for EU subsets, and cost target ~35% reduction vs current on-prem GPUs.
- Must-haves: token-based service auth (client-side SDK), per-customer routing policies, and support for structured tool-calling in the summary flow (fetch a ticket from the ClearHorizon API).

Action items I captured: 
1) Redwood to provide a reference SDK init snippet + auth flow and a candidate model-routing policy (p50-oriented + cost-tier fallback).
2) ClearHorizon to share sample traffic profile (seq lengths, qps by region) and security questionnaire follow-up.
3) Schedule a short tech sync to walk the SDK bootstrapping and the proposed fallback chain.

I attached a quick routing diagram and a draft SOW for visibility. Proposed times for the sync: Thu 8/5 9–10am PT or Fri 8/6 11–12pm PT. Please confirm.

Attachments: [attachment: redwood_routing_diagram.png (image/png)], [attachment: ClearHorizon_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks,

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. Quick clarifications before the sync: 

- Traffic profile: we will export a CSV of qps by endpoint and sample token lengths for the support-summarization traffic (our average sequence length today is ~320 tokens, heavy tail to 1500). Expect initial qps ~40, spiking to 120 during business hours.
- Residency: EU traffic must stay in eu-west (GDPR). US traffic OK in us-west or us-east.
- Cost target: the CFO asked for a clear quantification of how Redwood batching + fallback to smaller quantized models will hit the 35% savings target — can your team put numbers against a conservative and aggressive scenario?

Also, we want to understand structured tool calling support: the flow is: user -> summarization -> call to ClearHorizon ticket API to fetch full backstory -> rerun structured summary with ticket fields inserted. The summary must be able to call the ticket API reliably and then produce JSON (structured output) we can parse. Is that supported out of the box or do we need to add an orchestration layer?

Confirming Thu 8/5 9am PT works for the team.

—Alex

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ClearHorizon technical discovery — SDK setup, routing policies, and fallback options

Alex — high level technical follow-up before the sync with concrete pieces we'll bring. TL;DR: Redwood supports the flows you described; below are recommended config snippets and the fallback chain that matches your latency/cost goals.

1) SDK + auth (reference):
- Client SDK: lightweight JS + server-side Node helper for token refresh. Init pattern: Redwood.env('REDFLOW_KEY') for server, short-lived client tokens from your auth service.
- Auth modes: API keys (server-only), short-lived client bearer tokens (recommended for browser flows), and mutual TLS for Private deployments.
- Token scoping: issue per-customer scoped tokens so routing policies can split by tenant id.

2) Model routing policy (proposal):
- Primary route: r-instruct-4096-accelerated (balanced latency/quality) for p50 <= 150ms.
- Fallback tier A (cost saver): r-quant-3b for non-critical async rerank jobs and low priority batches.
- Fallback tier B (latency-first): r-lite-1.3b-ll for sub-30ms local inference in edge+cache scenarios.
- Policy rules: if sequence_length > 1024 OR structured_output_required == true -> prefer primary; if QPS spike > reserved_capacity_threshold -> route to fallback A for non-tool calls.

3) Structured tool-calling: supported via the Redwood SDK's function-calling primitives. We recommend the following pattern: 
- Step A: Summarize to extract ticket_id and a minimal context.
- Step B: Call ClearHorizon ticket API from app server.
- Step C: Re-prompt model with tool-filled context and request JSON schema output.
Redwood can do direct function/tool calling in hosted mode; for Private deployments you can still use the SDK hooks to validate tool results before final prompt.

4) Embeddings & reranker approach:
- Build a short-vector retriever (384d) for exact-match candidate generation.
- Use a dedicated reranker model (r-ranker-1.7b) to re-score top-k (k=20) — this should be routed to fallback A when cost pressure is high.
- Store per-tenant embedding namespaces; Redwood supports efficient per-namespace reranking and warmed KV caches.

5) Observability & cost control:
- We will provision token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency SLO dashboards.
- Autoscaling policies: reserve baseline capacity for business hours and set burst-to-dedicated for spikes to avoid cross-tenant throttle.

I'll bring a draft routing JSON and cost model (conservative/aggressive) to Thu's sync. Attaching the routing diagram Lauren shared for reference.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick security question ahead of the sync: does Redwood provide per-tenant audit logs (who requested what prompt / model / tokens) and can we forward those to our SIEM (SPLUNK) in near real-time? Our compliance team also needs confirmation that embedding vectors for EU tenants can be kept in the eu namespace only and never leave the region.

Also, CFO follow-up: any ballpark on the cost delta between primary route and fallback A per 1M tokens? Even a conservative ballpark will help with procurement.

Maya

Subject: Re: ClearHorizon technical discovery — SDK setup, routing policies, and fallback options

Perfect questions — see answers below and agenda for the sync at 9am PT in the calendar invite.

- Audit logs / SIEM: yes — Redwood streams per-request telemetry and structured audit logs. We support push integration to Splunk/BigQuery and can setup a near-real-time forwarder; logs include tenant_id, model_id, token_count, route_decision, and request metadata. (We'll scope retention in the SOW.)
- Embeddings residency: supported. For hosted customers we maintain region-scoped namespaces; for Private deployments we can enforce on-prem or VPC residency. We'll confirm config in the SOW.
- Cost delta (rough): primary route ~ $24 / 1M tokens (accelerated model), fallback A (quant-3b) ~ $9 / 1M tokens. These are conservative estimates — Aditya will validate with the cost model in the sync.

Agenda for 9am PT sync: 
1) Walk SDK init + auth patterns (10m) — Aditya
2) Routing policy JSON walkthrough + fallback decision tree (20m) — Aditya
3) Structured tool calling flow and example JSON schema (10m) — Stephanie
4) Embeddings + reranker sizing and namespace plan (10m) — Lauren
5) Next steps & SOW timeline (5m)

Next steps after sync: Aditya to send the routing policy JSON and two cost scenarios; Lauren to update SOW and include retention/region controls; ClearHorizon to provide sample traffic CSV.

Thanks — see you shortly.

Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
